text:
Sara Li: quick heads-up — batch #09 (labeling) has a huge duplicate rate. our golden set went from 520 -> 430 after dedupe step, but many of the removed items look like legit distinct examples. :thinking:
Priya Rao: can you paste a couple of examples? was this after the fingerprint change last week?
Sara Li: yes happened right after I merged the de-dupe fingerprint v2 PR. sample ids: S-00123, S-00157, S-00201. here's the fingerprint logic we used:```python
# naive fingerprint v2
def fingerprint(text):
    t = normalize_whitespace(text).lower()
    t = strip_soft_hyphens(t)
    return sha256(t.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
```
Matt O'Connor: hmm we changed normalization order in the runtime too (for quant tests) — could be a mismatch between onboarding pipeline and labeling pipeline canonicalizers. :eyes:
Ken Nakamura: @Sara Li can you run a quick compare between old v1 and v2 fingerprints on the golden set? a diff of hashes should reveal if it's canonicalization-only. I can also run a small script to detect near-duplicates (fuzzy) if it's tokenization drift.
Sara Li: running now, results: of 520 originals, 68 had hash collisions under v2 that weren't collisions under v1. attaching tiny diff (id, v1, v2): S-00123,a1f3...,b3f3...; S-00157,c9d2...,c9d2... (same); S-00201,e8a1...,e8a1... (same) — so some changed, some stable.
Jasmine Alvarez: we also saw a spike in labeling disagreements on conversational turns in the same batch — labeler comments said "utterance trimmed" for a few examples. Could be whitespace/softbreak handling.
Labeler Bot: Automated note — 14 labelers flagged 'context-trim' in batch #09. Queue: 14/120 flagged.
Priya Rao: this matches a quantization experiment where the tokenization mapping was run through the new tokenizer heuristics (qtest branch). If token boundaries change, fingerprinting that relies on normalized text will disagree. We need to decide: (A) snap canonicalizer across pipelines, or (B) make dedupe tolerant (token aware).
Ken Nakamura: preference A for immediate stability. short term: revert to v1 canonicalizer in the labeling pipeline and reprocess the batch. medium term: add token-aware dedupe with fuzzy threshold. I'll open an infra ticket.
Matt O'Connor: re: quant experiments — EvalBot just posted a regression for q4_small on conversational coherence. Maybe the tokenizer tweaks caused both the perf deltas and the dedupe mismatch.
EvalBot: [AUTOMATED] Regression alert: model q4_small (2027-03-18) increased response perplexity on conv-bench by +7.4%. Linked eval: https://redwood.internal/evals/7845 :zap:
Sara Li: plan: 1) revert labeling pipeline canonicalizer to v1 and re-run dedupe on batch #09 (Ken/Matt) 2) collect a diff report and mark 68 suspect items for manual review (Priya/Jasmine) 3) lock golden set until manual review complete 4) add a CI check: canonicalizer hash parity between onboarding/runtime/labeling. I'll start reprocessing and post updates.
Priya Rao: I can take the manual review tonight — will prioritize the ones with hash divergence + labeler flags. estimated 2-3 hours.
Jasmine Alvarez: I'll update the labeling guideline doc to explicitly call out soft-hyphen and trailing space rules so labelers have context. tiny PR incoming. :memo:
Matt O'Connor: also recommend adding a small script to compare tokenizations across branches: `python tools/token_diff.py --ids S-00123,S-00201` — saves future guesswork.
Ken Nakamura: ticket created: INFRA-1289 "canonicalizer parity + dedupe tolerance". Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml. ETA initial patch tomorrow.
Sara Li: thanks team. ping me here with manual review results. I'll hold golden set updates until we confirm. :lock: 
Priya Rao: will report by 2200 PST.
Labeler Bot: Batch #09 reprocessing queued (job 4521). ETA ~12m.
Sara Li: reprocess done — preliminary: dedupe removals reduced from 90 -> 22 after revert. posting final list now.
Matt O'Connor: awesome, that's much better. follow-up: let's run the quant tokenizer tests in a sandbox before merging anything that touches normalization.
Jasmine Alvarez: PR for labeling guideline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/labeling/pull/412 — small clarifications added.
Ken Nakamura: closing note: add a quick `sha-check` step in CI that fails if hash drift > 0.1% on golden sample. I'll add to INFRA-1289.
Sara Li: closing the thread — golden set is locked, manual review in progress, thanks y'all :pray:
